exposure: MRI sequence combinations (T1WI + T2WI; T1WI + T2WI + DWI; T1WI + T2WI + DCE-MRI; T2WI + DWI + DCE-MRI)
MRI classifications of Cesarean scar pregnancy (Type I, II, III)
outcome: Clinical value of MRI in classifying CSP
Diagnostic performance (sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value, negative predictive value, AUC)
Imaging features of CSP types (length of contact surface, minimum scar thickness, gestational sac area)
cohort: 80 patients with suspected Cesarean scar pregnancy (CSP) identified by ultrasound examination, confirmed by postoperative pathology.
finding: The preferred MRI sequence combination for diagnosing Cesarean scar pregnancy (CSP) is T2WI + DWI + DCE-MRI, demonstrating superior diagnostic performance (e.g., AUC up to 0.979), and MRI effectively visualizes the relationship between the gestational sac and the incisional diverticulum, facilitating imaging-based staging of CSP.
